plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: Ruffled cups of saturated colour stand in ruler-straight rows across the Dutch bulb fields. From the air, the fields look like stripes of crimson, butter yellow and violet laid across the flat green land. Tulips are also a staple of home flower beds and big public gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: April into early May. In the Netherlands, the show typically peaks in the last two weeks of April and the first week of May.
plants.location: The Netherlands, including the bulb fields and Keukenhof gardens near Lisse
plants.funFact: In the 1630s, tulip bulbs became so prized in the Dutch Republic that single bulbs sold for the price of a fine house. The episode is remembered as 'tulip mania', one of history's earliest speculative bubbles.

plants.name: Wisteria floribunda
plants.description: Wisteria hangs in long, fragrant, waterfall-like clusters of lilac flowers. Trained over pergolas and trellises in Japanese gardens, it forms glowing purple tunnels that hum with bees. Its sweet scent drifts well beyond the vines.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-April to mid-May. Flowering begins in the warmer south, and the main show falls around early May in much of Japan.
plants.location: Japan, in temple and park gardens such as those found across Honshu and Kyushu
plants.funFact: Wisteria is a twining climber, and Japanese wisteria twists clockwise as it climbs. Old vines can grow heavy and thick enough to crush the structures they are trained over.

plants.name: Rhododendron arboreum
plants.description: This is a gnarled Himalayan tree that erupts in blood-red, pink and white blossom clusters, turning whole misty hillsides into a blaze of colour. It is the national flower of Nepal. Trekkers walk beneath its canopy through forests in the mountains.
plants.bloomingSeason: March to May. Lower slopes bloom first, and the higher elevations continue into late April and early May.
plants.location: The Himalayan foothills and mountain forests of Nepal, roughly 1,500 to 4,000 metres in elevation
plants.funFact: Nepal is home to about 30 rhododendron species, more than any other country. The petals of the tree rhododendron are edible and are used in local cooking and traditional drinks.
